trials.label: r1c1
trials.name: set A reference
trials.hypothesis: Reference net with summed layouts A = {identity, transpose, y-flip, x-flip}. This covers a world whose actions are transposed or flipped on one axis relative to the obs. Scores of 0.15 or more would mean the true layout is in A, and round 2 splits it. A 0 here while set B scores would rule out A's deviations.

trials.label: r1c2
trials.name: set B reference
trials.hypothesis: Reference net with summed layouts B = {y+x-flip, transpose+y-flip, transpose+x-flip, transpose+y+x-flip}. This covers rotations and the anti-transpose. A nonzero score, especially with set A at 0, would place the true layout in B. If every candidate scores 0, layouts alone are not the fix.

trials.label: r1c3
trials.name: set A + obs symmetries
trials.hypothesis: Set A, with the obs concatenated under all 8 grid symmetries in the stem. This targets an obs reoriented relative to both the actions and the mask (worlds 1, 5). If this scores where plain set A scores 0, the obs frame is off, and round 2 splits the obs views. Equal scores would mean the obs views are not needed.

trials.label: r1c4
trials.name: set B + obs symmetries
trials.hypothesis: Set B, with the obs fed under all 8 grid symmetries. This covers rotated action layouts combined with a reoriented obs. It scoring while plain set B scores 0 would show an obs-frame deviation outside set A. All four layout candidates scoring 0 would rule out simple dihedral misalignment as the only problem.

trials.label: r1c5
trials.name: set A + LayerNorm stems
trials.hypothesis: Set A with separate obs and mask stems, per-cell LayerNorm in the stems and trunk, and output layers at orthogonal gain 0.01. This targets inputs on an unexpected scale, as in world 4. Scoring where plain set A scores 0 would point to an input-scale deviation. A 0 when another candidate scores would mean LayerNorm is not the bottleneck.

trials.label: r1c6
trials.name: set A + obs sym + LayerNorm
trials.hypothesis: Combines set A, the 8 obs symmetries, LayerNorm stems and trunk, and gain-0.01 outputs. This covers a world with both a reoriented obs and an input-scale deviation. If only this candidate scores, both hedges are needed, and round 2 removes each in turn. If simpler candidates score as well, this combination adds nothing.

trials.label: r2c1
trials.name: combo A type-major
trials.hypothesis: Set A (type-major) plus 8 obs symmetries, LayerNorm stems and trunk, gain-0.01 outputs, global context in each residual block and a dilated residual block. This is step 5's combined hedge: it fixes the scale and receptive-field problems that may have blocked set A even when a layout was right. A nonzero score means the plain hedges lacked these extras, and round 3 splits A. A 0 while the type-minor or B combos score refutes it.

trials.label: r2c2
trials.name: combo B type-major
trials.hypothesis: Same combined hedge as combo A, but with set B (rotations and anti-transpose). Round 1 never tried set B with LayerNorm, so a B layout combined with an input-scale deviation is still open. A nonzero score here, with combo A at 0, places the layout in B and calls for a split. A 0 while the type-minor or dense candidates score refutes it.

trials.label: r2c3
trials.name: combo A type-minor
trials.hypothesis: Same combined hedge as combo A, but the mask and output are read type-minor: action = (y*X+x)*K + t. If the world interleaves brick types per cell, every round-1 net misread both the mask and the logits. A nonzero score here, with the type-major combos at 0, confirms type-minor ordering, as in world 3. A 0 here and on type-minor B rules out type-minor ordering with dihedral frames.

trials.label: r2c4
trials.name: combo B type-minor
trials.hypothesis: Type-minor action ordering (type innermost) under set B frames, with obs symmetries, LayerNorm, global context and a dilated block. Together with type-minor A, this covers all 8 dihedral frames in type-minor order. A nonzero score here, with type-minor A at 0, locates the layout in type-minor B. Zeros on all four combos would rule out the dihedral × ordering family and point to a non-dihedral remap or a reward deviation.

trials.label: r2c5
trials.name: combo A + dense action remap
trials.hypothesis: Combo A plus a learned dense remap. A Linear embeds the full mask, including DONE, into per-cell maps. A Linear from the flattened head features and global features adds into all logits, including DONE. Together these can learn arbitrary action permutations, such as DONE at index 0 or shifted anchors. If only this candidate scores, the deviation is not dihedral, and round 3 strengthens the dense path. A 0 while other candidates score means the remap is unnecessary.

trials.label: r2c6
trials.name: combo A + separate critic
trials.hypothesis: Combo A with a small separate LayerNorm critic, gamma 0.99 and ent_coef 0.01. This targets a reward or credit deviation, such as delayed or rescaled reward, under which the shared critic at gamma 0.9 never learns the exact-build bonus. Scoring where combo A scores 0 points to a credit problem. A lower score than combo A when both score refutes it, consistent with earlier harm from gamma ≥0.97.

trials.label: r3c1
trials.name: clean dihedral single layout
trials.hypothesis: Uses only the identity mask/output layout, the obs under 8 symmetries, LayerNorm stems and trunk, global context and gain-0.01 outputs. With no summed output layouts, it covers all 8 dihedral obs-action relations with no interference between layouts. Earlier zeros may have come from summing layouts. A score of 0.15 or more locates the deviation among the obs views, to be split in round 4. A 0 here, together with the earlier results, rules out the dihedral family.

trials.label: r3c2
trials.name: learned token mixing
trials.hypothesis: Adds two residual token-mixing layers, each a learned Linear across the Y·X cells, to the clean dihedral net. These can learn any fixed spatial permutation between the obs and the actions, such as rolls, anchor shifts larger than the receptive field, or shuffled cells. Convs and obs symmetries cannot cover these. If this scores while candidate 1 scores 0, the remap is not dihedral. If both score 0, a spatial remap is refuted.

trials.label: r3c3
trials.name: instance-norm input path
trials.hypothesis: Adds a stem path to the clean dihedral net. A learned depthwise 1x1 conv acts on each obs view, then each channel is instance-normalised over the grid and fed to the stem. This removes per-channel constant offsets and rescales each channel. Per-cell LayerNorm cannot remove an offset that dominates every cell, which would explain why the earlier LayerNorm hedge in r1c5 did not work. If this scores while candidate 1 scores 0, the inputs are offset or scaled per channel. A 0 refutes that.

trials.label: r3c4
trials.name: DONE at index 0
trials.hypothesis: The clean dihedral net, but it reads actions as DONE at index 0 and placements at 1..n_place. The mask is read from those indices and the DONE logit is written first. If DONE sits first, every earlier net misplaced DONE and shifted all placements by one index, so it could neither stop nor aim reliably. If this scores while candidate 1 scores 0, the action index is offset. If it scores 0 while candidate 1 scores, the offset hypothesis is refuted.

trials.label: r3c5
trials.name: dense MLP action path
trials.hypothesis: Adds a full-scale MLP to the clean dihedral net. It reads the flattened raw obs and the full mask, passes them through a 256-unit LayerNorm hidden layer, and adds its output to every logit, including DONE, and to the value. Unlike the weak r2c5 remap, which saw only 4 features per cell, this path sees the raw obs, so it can learn arbitrary scrambles of the obs or actions. If this scores while the conv-only candidates score 0, the scramble is non-local. A 0 refutes it.

trials.label: r3c6
trials.name: channels-last obs reading
trials.hypothesis: Adds a second reading of the obs memory to the clean dihedral net: reshape to (Y, X, C), then permute to channels-first. Both readings go into the stem under the 8 symmetries. If the world stores the obs channels-last but declares it [C, Y, X], every channel earlier nets saw was scrambled, and no layout or LayerNorm hedge could fix it. If this scores while candidate 1 scores 0, the obs memory layout is wrong. A 0 refutes that.

trials.label: r4c1
trials.name: long-horizon credit recipe
trials.hypothesis: Keeps the clean dihedral net but uses gamma 0.99, gae_lambda 0.95 and ent_coef 0.01. This targets sparse or delayed reward, where gamma 0.9 and lambda 0.85 cannot carry credit back to early placements. Unlike r2c6, the net is light, so it gets more samples, the critic is shared, and lambda is higher. A score above 0 points to a credit deviation. A 0 refutes delayed reward as the only problem.

trials.label: r4c2
trials.name: isolated scale-free critic
trials.hypothesis: Adds a separate small LayerNorm critic with a learnable output scale, exp(log_scale). Its value gradient is scaled by 0.05 through a detach trick: Adam still learns it at full rate, but it barely counts in the global grad-norm clip. This targets a reward on an unexpected scale, where a huge value loss swamps the shared trunk and the clip. The recipe stays at gamma 0.9, unlike r2c6. A score above 0 points to reward scale. A 0 refutes it.

trials.label: r4c3
trials.name: three obs memory readings
trials.hypothesis: Feeds the obs memory read three ways, as (C,Y,X), (Y,X,C) and the untested (Y,C,X), each under 8 symmetries, so axis-swapped versions are covered too. This targets an obs whose storage order differs from its declared shape, which would scramble every channel the earlier nets saw. r3c6 covered only the channels-last reading. A score above 0 points to an obs memory-layout deviation. A 0 rules out every axis-order reinterpretation of the obs.

trials.label: r4c4
trials.name: mask under all frames
trials.hypothesis: Feeds the mask, read both type-major and type-minor, under all 8 symmetries (16 mask views), while the output keeps the identity layout. This targets a mask frame that differs from both the obs and the actions. No earlier net gave the stem every mask frame next to every obs frame, so legality cues may have been misaligned. A score above 0 points to a mask-frame deviation. A 0 refutes it.

trials.label: r4c5
trials.name: strong exploration recipe
trials.hypothesis: Keeps the clean dihedral net but uses ent_coef 0.03, clip_eps 0.3, gamma 0.95 and gae_lambda 0.95. This targets a world where reward is hard to reach, for example shaping that is weaker or penalised, so near-greedy policies with low entropy settle on degenerate behaviour, such as DONE at once, before any exact build. A score above 0 points to an exploration bottleneck. A 0, alongside the credit candidate, refutes recipe-only fixes.

trials.label: r4c6
trials.name: kitchen-sink final hedge
trials.hypothesis: Combines the three obs memory readings × 8 symmetries, 16 mask views, the isolated scale-free critic, and gamma 0.97, gae_lambda 0.95 and ent_coef 0.01. This is a last-round bet that the world stacks several untested deviations, as in world 3, where only a combination escaped. If it scores alone, the deviations are compound. If a single-hedge candidate scores higher, the extras cost samples. A 0 everywhere means the deviation lies outside what an architecture can fix.

analyses.1: There are no results yet, and the starting net scores 0. Earlier searches found that a 0 like this usually comes from a frame mismatch between the obs and the action/mask layout. Changing the recipe or capacity alone never fixed it. Round 1 follows the program. I test layout set A and set B as 4-way summed hedges. Each set is also tried with the obs fed under all 8 grid symmetries, which targets an obs that is reoriented relative to the actions (as in worlds 1 and 5). Two more candidates add per-cell LayerNorm stems and trunk with gain-0.01 outputs, which targets inputs on an unexpected scale (as in world 4). All six use the reference recipe and keep r between about 1.0 and 1.2. Any nonzero score marks the set and hedges to split in round 2. If all six score 0, the reference layouts and obs views are probably not enough. Round 2 would then combine hedges and try type-minor layouts.
analyses.4: All 18 trials scored 0 on dev, and none had any training success. The frame hedges are ruled out: dihedral layouts A and B, read type-major or type-minor, and the obs under 8 symmetries. So are input-scale fixes (LayerNorm, instance norm), learned token mixing, DONE at index 0, a dense MLP path and channels-last obs. The separate critic at gamma 0.99 failed too, but that test was confounded with a heavy combined net. Since nothing ever learned, the remaining causes lie outside the action layout: reward credit or scale, the obs memory layout (Y,C,X is untested), or the mask's frame. All candidates in this last round start from the clean dihedral net from r3c1: identity output, obs under 8 symmetries, LayerNorm and global context. Each tests one untested cause: long-horizon credit, a gradient-isolated critic for odd reward scale, three obs memory readings, mask views under every frame, strong exploration, and one kitchen-sink combination. Any nonzero score beats the starting net.
